$comment: Every test suite this repository has, and whether a pull request's CI runs it. scripts/test-coverage.mjs fails CI when a package.json script, a directory under tests/ or a test config is missing from this file, and posts the suites marked notOnPr on every pull request, so a green check never claims a suite it did not run.

pnpm exec tsc --noEmit.what: The frontend typechecks. tsconfig.json includes src only, so nothing under tests/ or scripts/ is covered (AGENTS.md, 'the other hand-maintained ports').
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit.notAScript: CI typechecks without building. The `build` script is `tsc && vite build`, and the vite build runs only inside the installer.

test.what: The data-layer workflow harness: the real migrations loaded into in-memory SQLite, the lab-pipeline invariants, and a gate per GitHub issue.

test:scenarios.what: The lab-record logic on this tree's real src/lib/db.ts, in Node, on a real SQLite file (tests/scenarios): A2's staining-rack model (slides entering staining pool into one rack per agent across samples, which replaces the retired test:staining), H1's Logs export pinned cell by cell (all four notes under their on-screen labels, plus the slide's own note), and A1's open issues #144 and #148, each marked it.fails so CI stays green until the fix lands and goes red if the marker outlives it. #139 is fixed and a hard check, and A3's route sweep (retraction-routes.test.ts) walks every route that takes a cut back out of a group or puts work on glass never cut, asserting on the invariant in invariants.ts (no live slide carries a work stamp without a cut date). #146's data-layer proof (signed-out-restore.test.ts) is a hard check: a restore with nobody signed in is refused and no restore changes who is signed in. #150's data-layer proof (mass-imaging.test.ts) is a hard check: slides marked imaged in one action each carry their own stamp and audit record, a never-cut slide is refused and left untouched while the rest are marked, and a signed-out call is refused, and drag-to-imaging.test.ts is a hard check that a group waiting in Needs Sectioning cannot go straight to Ready for Imaging while every ordinary forward move still works. The undo journal's own proofs are hard checks on the real db.ts: undo-journal.test.ts round-trips a journal replay across every table, row for row and rowid for rowid, including the steps whose deletes cascade; undo-lane.test.ts fires a save and an Undo in one gesture, with no await between them, and asserts the Undo takes back that save rather than the one before it (the undo-vs-save race; save-vs-save is tests/e2e/undo-races.spec.ts); revert-clears-undo.test.ts asserts a revert to a backup empties both stacks and leaves the safety backup it took first; and journal-retention.test.ts relaunches a lab to prove the journal is trimmed at open to its five-megabyte ceiling, and by its secondary row-count and age guards, and left exactly as it is while it is inside the bound. undo-sync-drain.test.ts drives the real githubSync.ts drain against the shared fake remote, and the app's own actions through useActions: a viewer's request drained between an Undo and the Redo of it makes the redo refuse with nothing changed instead of restoring the block's whole row over it; an undo leaves alone a request drained after the action it takes back, and an assay Settings added meanwhile; a refused undo or redo is skipped in one sentence and the step before it is still reachable, so a refusal cannot wedge the stack, whether the replay was blocked by a guard or by a constraint on a key something else has taken, while a replay that fails for any other reason keeps its step and says to try again;  and the drain waits for the write lane rather than writing inside somebody else's action.

test:legacy.what: A real populated pre-0023 database, taken up both upgrade paths.

test:ui.what: Component and render tests under jsdom. vitest.config.ts includes src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} only.

test:e2e.what: The real app in Chromium against the sql.js Tauri shim: read-only gating, drawer state, filters, the request dialog, everything above the data layer. E4's guard (scripts/no-unasserted-captures.mjs) keeps captures out of this directory; retries are 0 (playwright.config.ts), so a pass here means first attempt, not eventually. undo-races.spec.ts drives the two undo races through the real toolbar and editors; it is only evidence because the shim's IPC-cost knob (window.__SNAPSHOT_IPC_MS__, src/test/browser-core-shim.ts) gives read_file and save_file the time they take on a lab-sized database, without which the window closes in a microtask and the specs pass on any code.

render.what: pnpm verify's render layer: the pull request's base and this tree served side by side, the same small lab built on both, ARIA structure diffed and layout/contrast audited at two widths - the screenshot comparison without a screenshot or a stored baseline (tests/render/).
render.notAScript: Invoked by scripts/verify.mjs, which builds and serves both trees itself; there is no standalone pnpm script for it.

test:screenshot.what: The 26 captures E4 moved out of tests/e2e (2026-09-14 review), so a person can still look. Every flow here is already proven correct by its tests/e2e companion's assertions; this tier exists only to produce the images.

test:compat.what: The release in use and this tree, each opening, working on, reverting and syncing the other's database (docs/release_compat.md).

test:release.what: The release checks' own tests, and that this tree's five version sources agree. The same workflow also runs `release-check.mjs provenance`, which is a check on the repository rather than a suite.

test:suites.what: This file checked against the tree and the workflows, and the checker's own tests.

cargo test --lib --locked.what: The Rust shell, and in it db_migrate_image (src-tauri/src/migrate.rs) and the two undo-journal commands (src-tauri/src/undo_journal.rs: one all-or-nothing transaction for a journal replay and for installing the triggers), which the TypeScript models in src/test/sqlx-migrator.ts and src/test/undoJournalCommands.ts only stand in for, and the file logic of backups and restore (src-tauri/src/backup_fs.rs: validated, atomic, name-guarded writes, listing, pruning), run on temporary directories. The same job runs `cargo check --locked` first, which is what catches a version bumped in Cargo.toml and not in Cargo.lock.
cargo test --lib --locked.notAScript: The Rust shell is built by cargo, not by pnpm; the job runs it in src-tauri.

bash scripts/backup-mutants.sh.what: The proof the backup_fs tests can fail: plants 20 defects one at a time in a copy of src-tauri/src/backup_fs.rs (a bypassed magic check, a name carrying a slash, backslash or .., a copy in place of the atomic rename, a skipped sweep, listing or pruning from the wrong end) and fails when any survives every test. Std only, so it needs no Tauri build.
bash scripts/backup-mutants.sh.notAScript: A shell script that drives cargo, run by the rust job after cargo test.

test:stress.what: The v1 stress walk that remains after 01 to 05 were retired (superseded by test:stress2 and test:stress3): 06-durability and 07-bench-reality, with retries off and console errors fatal.
test:stress.notOnPr: It is slow and fills the database up rather than proving one behaviour, so it stays out of the path that gates every push.

test:stress2.what: Scale and invariants: a seeded random walk of thousands of data-layer actions, fuzzed interleavings, sentinel values, and an invariant set derived from defects that were real.
test:stress2.notOnPr: It is minutes long (about 12 idle) and peaks near 11 GB of memory, so it stays out of the path that gates every push.

test:stress3.what: The explorer: the walk of v2 driven through the real UI, with each surface compared against a count recomputed from the store, plus Undo and Redo (docs/stress_test_v3.md).
test:stress3.notOnPr: It drives the browser for minutes, so it stays out of the path that gates every push.

playwright test --config playwright.show.what: The tutorial and screenshot walkthrough: it photographs the app's screens for a person to look at.
playwright test --config playwright.show.notAScript: It has no package.json script; the config's own header says to run it with `npx playwright test --config playwright.showcase.config.ts`.
playwright test --config playwright.show.notOnPr: It is kept out of the main suite on purpose so it never gates a release, and it takes screenshots rather than asserting behaviour.

otherScripts.dev: The Vite dev server against the Tauri shell.
otherScripts.dev:browser: The Vite dev server with the sql.js Tauri shim, which every Playwright suite serves.
otherScripts.build: tsc && vite build. CI typechecks with `tsc --noEmit`; the vite build itself runs only inside the installer build, as tauri.conf.json's beforeBuildCommand.
otherScripts.test:e2e:headed: The end-to-end suite with a visible browser, for local work.
otherScripts.test:e2e:ui: The end-to-end suite in Playwright's UI mode, for local work.
otherScripts.verify: The layered gate (scripts/verify.mjs): data, render, e2e, then (--screenshot) the screenshot tier, cheapest first, stopping at the first red layer. Not a suite of its own; it runs the suites already listed above.

otherPaths.tests/fixtures: Recorded databases the suites read; tests/fixtures/legacy-pre-0023.b64 is test:legacy's input.
otherPaths.tests/helpers: Page helpers shared by the Playwright suites.
